metadata.title: Post-Closing Integration: A Plan, or a Tracker?
metadata.purpose: Answer what a team should build the day an M&A deal closes: a one-time integration plan, or a live phased tracker. Lands the carry-out that you can't manage an integration you're not tracking -- the tracker has to outlast the plan.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet's narration carried unfilled '>' template placeholders at every skill-specific fact, and its named source_skill file does not exist on this machine -- see QUESTION.md. This redo reconstructs a generic, defensible integration-tracking account from the one real phrase the source did contain ('post-closing M&A integration tracker -- phased workplan') rather than lifting facts that were never written.

beats.narration_text: Someone whose deal just closed asks if they need a master integration plan. Wrong first word. What they actually need is a tracker -- a phased workplan. Liam, take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Do we need a plan for after the deal closes?', hesitates on 'plan', corrects to 'tracker', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('plan' -> 'tracker') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: You could write an integration plan the day the deal closes -- a single document listing what has to happen. But a plan captures one moment; the day after closing, workstreams start moving in parallel -- IT, HR, finance, contracts -- and a static document can't tell you which ones are on schedule and which have quietly stalled. What actually closes that gap isn't a plan, it's a live tracker.

shot.new_visual_element: A sealed 'plan' document card listing named workstreams; a fourth, unlabeled workstream sliding in beneath it, unmarked and unlit

production_viz.label: A plan only lists what's named on day one
production_viz.mechanic: A card labelled 'INTEGRATION PLAN' with a wax-seal glyph and three named workstream chips inside it, fully lit. A fourth chip slides in from below the card, dim and unlit, passing underneath without touching the plan card. A caption fades in beneath: 'the plan never knew it existed.'

beats.narration_text: Four things go in for every workstream on that tracker: the task, the owner, the target phase -- day-one, day-thirty, day-one-hundred -- and today's status. Watch the anchor: the vendor-contract workstream marked day-thirty on the org chart, with no owner ever assigned to it.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- four field chips lighting in turn (task / owner / phase / status), then a dim, unlabeled workstream card set off to the side

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- four fields, then the unowned workstream
production_viz.mechanic: Four chips fade in one at a time across the top, each labelled with a field (task / owner / phase / status), then fade out together. THE ANCHOR. A single card appears off to the side, dim and outlined only, reading 'vendor contracts -- day 30' with no owner field filled in -- visibly incomplete against the four-field shape just shown. THIS EXACT CARD RETURNS, FILLED IN, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: That workstream gets the same four fields as everything else -- owner assigned, phase set, status tracked -- and now it's visible instead of silently late. But 'in progress' doesn't mean on schedule; status is a snapshot, not a guarantee. And a fully staffed tracker on day one doesn't mean nothing else surfaces -- new workstreams turn up as integration proceeds.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- the dim card lighting up with all four fields filled and sliding into the main tracker; then split into 'tracked is not on schedule' and 'staffed is not complete'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- tracked, not cleared
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 DIM CARD RETURNS, identical placement, and fills in one field at a time (task / owner / phase / status) until fully lit, then slides into a row alongside other tracked workstreams. It splits into two cards: left reads 'status: in progress' with a struck-through 'ON SCHEDULE' beneath it labelled 'tracked is not on schedule'; right reads 'tracker: staffed today' with a faint new unlabeled card appearing at its edge labelled 'staffed is not complete'.

beats.narration_text: You can't manage an integration you're not tracking. Build the phased tracker, not a single plan -- the plan only holds for day one.

props.quote: You can't manage an integration you're not tracking. Build the phased tracker, not a single plan -- the plan only holds for day one.
props.sparkLine: Tracker first, then the plan holds.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt -- read it with me. List the workstreams for a hypothetical post-closing integration -- IT systems, HR and benefits, finance consolidation, vendor contracts. For each one, assign an owner and a target phase: day-one, day-thirty, or day-one-hundred. Mark today's status. If any workstream has no owner, that's the gap the tracker just found. Liam, in for Bear.
